title: Coming in the next release
improved: In progress: Admin > Data Updates (a schedule for every outside data set) and fixed-wing air ambulances

title: ArkSignal: new name, home page, menus, hospitals, air ambulances and more
added: Coverage Map (/coverage): one map with a layer for each kind of service: ADS-B coverage around every station, MLAT stations, and UAT / ADS-R traffic right now. More layers join it as the network grows
Choose the page you land on after signing in (Profile > After I sign in, take me to), with a site default set by an administrator in Settings > Accounts. A page you were heading to still wins
The How to Feed section is split into pages with a sub-menu: ADS-B, MLAT, UAT (978 MHz) and Am I Feeding?. Old links keep working
Settings are grouped into tabs (General, Accounts and Security, Map and Data, Feeders and Alerts, Updates and Backups) with a search box that finds a setting by name

The network is now called ArkSignal. The header wordmark, page titles (Page | ArkSignal), About, emails and the Feed and Support wording follow it; the name, accent part and tagline are settings (Admin > Settings > General), and adsb.allisononline.org keeps working
A rewritten About page: what the network is, who runs it (a hobby project run by two volunteers), what you can do here today, where it is going, and credits for the MLAT server, Planefence and rclone

A new home page: ArkSignal at a glance, with a live strip (aircraft overhead, stations online, MLAT, service status), a map preview, one search box for a callsign, tail number, airport, city or station, a card for each service and the latest release. The previous home page is now Aircraft Tracking (/aircraft, also in the menu)

Moving to arksignal.allisononline.org: an administrator can set a Main Address and a list of Old Addresses (Settings > General) so page requests on the old address are sent to the new one with a permanent redirect; it stays off until it is filled in

Search the live map by place: type a city, ZIP code or county in the map search box and pick it from the list (or press Enter) to jump there. The places come from the US Census Bureau and are loaded by an administrator under Admin > Places

Hospitals: a public Hospitals list and a page for each hospital (address, emergency care, trauma level and services where known, and the heliport it uses), a Hospitals layer on the live map coloured by trauma level, and an Admin > Hospitals page that loads the list from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services and finds each hospital with the Census Bureau geocoder. Trauma levels, services and heliport links are entered by an administrator and kept by every update

Air ambulance helicopters: an Air ambulance entry in the live map's Aircraft Type filter (count, chip, and a line on the aircraft card naming the operator). They are found from the aircraft database tar1090 uses (helicopters owned by Air Evac, Air Methods, Med-Trans, Life Flight Network, REACH, hospitals and similar) plus a tail number list an administrator keeps in Admin > Air Ambulance

Import trauma levels: Admin > Hospitals takes a CSV list of trauma-designated hospitals (with a preview), matches it to the hospitals by position and name, adds the ones the public list lacks, and shows the level, designation date and source on each hospital page
A map legend on the live map: a collapsible panel that explains the colours of whatever layers are switched on

Administrators can open any account (Admin > Users, click a name) and change what the person can change themselves: email address, display name, callsign, display choices and landing page, alert webhook and alert rules, and sign-ins, with two-factor reset, a temporary password and unlock. The current password is never shown to anyone, only replaced; every change is written to the audit log, and only a Super Admin can change a Super Admin

Hospital filters: choose which kinds of facility are loaded (acute care, critical access, children's, rural emergency, Veterans Administration, Department of Defense, psychiatric, long-term), leave out names containing words such as BEHAVIORAL or SURGICAL, and optionally keep only hospitals with an emergency department. Behavioral health centres are out by default, and an update removes loaded facilities that no longer match (anything edited by hand is kept)

Hospital services: stroke, neurosurgery, cardiac, obstetrics, NICU, children's, burn, orthopedics, cancer and psychiatric tags on hospitals, a Service filter on the Hospitals list, and a CSV import that can carry them (with the CMS number for exact matching). The hospital import now keeps only hospitals with an emergency department by default
improved: The top menu and a slim bottom bar (About, Status, Release Notes, Roadmap, Contact) stay in view while you scroll long pages, on phones too
Search boxes on the admin Users, Feeders, MLAT and Map Layers lists, and on the public Feeders page; click a column heading to sort
Flights, Flight History and Airports can be sorted by any column
New stations are shown feed.arksignal.allisononline.org on the How to Feed page; stations already using feed.adsb.allisononline.org keep working and the page says so

The top menu is grouped by service: Aircraft (map, flights, history, airports, MLAT, tools), Network (coverage, stations, statistics, status) and Feed, with the part of the site you are in highlighted; new services get their own group as they arrive

Inside Aircraft, Network or Feed a second bar under the top menu lists that service's pages with the current one marked; clicking a group name goes to that section, and resting the mouse on it opens its menu
Live map: every filter that is on shows as a small chip you can click to switch it off, with a Clear All button
The top menu and the section bar now run the full width of the window and fold into a menu button on narrow screens instead of being cut off

Hospitals on the live map are square badges instead of dots: the trauma level number on a colour for trauma centres, a red plus for an emergency department, grey for none, and a blue H where a heliport is linked, so they stand apart from airports
Airport weather on the live map now refreshes by itself every few minutes (the weather refresh setting) instead of only when the map is moved

adsb.allisononline.org now sends visitors to arksignal.allisononline.org (page requests only; the feed and MLAT addresses are untouched). The Main Address and the list of old addresses are in Settings > General
fixed: Hospital markers on the live map can be clicked, like the airports
The admin user page uses one consistent width and shows the user name as plain text

title: Planefence, off-site backups, live release notes and roadmap
added: Planefence and Plane-Alert: which aircraft flew over Arkansas, with photos, airlines and routes, and a list of interesting aircraft (military, government, rare); in the Tools menu, with notifications (Discord, Mastodon and others) set up on an administrator-only configuration page. It arrives with Update Now, with no files to edit by hand

Off-site backups: Admin > Backups > Off-Site Copy sends encrypted copies of everything (the portal database with all flights and history, the hub's secret keys and settings, Grafana, statistics history and the hub's traffic history) to an SFTP server, S3 bucket, NAS share or WebDAV, with a small daily copy and a big weekly copy as separate files, connection test, copy-now buttons and a history of runs

Restore Part: restore only some areas of a backup (accounts, stations, flight history, alerts, settings...), or bring back one person, station, role or alert rule with what belongs to it, in merge or replace mode, with a safety backup first. The off-site restore helper can also unpack only chosen parts
Aircraft Type filter on the live map: helicopters, jets, turboprops, piston props, large and heavy, light aircraft, gliders and balloons, drones, ground vehicles and unknown type, with counts
A public Roadmap page (/roadmap): what is coming next, in progress, planned and just released, filterable by area

Live Release Notes and Roadmap: both pages read their lists from the project's repository, so they update as soon as work is pushed instead of staying frozen at the last release (Admin > Updates > Live Content)

A Support page (hidden until an administrator sets it up in Admin > Support): why donations help, what the network costs to run with a monthly progress bar, links to Ko-fi and PayPal, and an Equipment Fund wish list for antennas, receivers and mesh nodes the project installs at host sites. The portal only links out and never handles payment details
improved: The keyboard shortcuts help opens as a popup in the middle of the screen, on top of everything
Registration, change password, reset and forgot-password forms list their requirements and tick them as you type, including user name rules, email format and whether the two passwords match

Every section of the live map's filters (Stations, Show, Data Source, Aircraft Flags, Aircraft Type, Altitude, Display and View, Layers) folds up like the sections of the aircraft details card, remembers whether you left it open, and shows a small count of the filters active in it
fixed: Am I Feeding said MLAT was not connected for a claimed station even when it was working

title: Live map upgrades, MLAT user names, release notes
added: MLAT User Name on the station page: stations that already use a different MLAT_USER are recognised by it (the Station ID is used when it is empty)
Units on the live map: aeronautical (ft, kt, nm), metric or imperial, chosen per visitor with a site default in Settings
Keyboard shortcuts on the live map with the same keys as tar1090 (F, I, U, V, L, O, K, B, R, H, Q, E, arrows, / and ?), plus a help panel
Search on the live map takes several terms with commas, * wildcards and ! to leave terms out, and also matches squawk and model
Aircraft Flags filter (military, interesting, PIA, LADD) in the live map's filter card
Jump to a place: type coordinates, an aircraft hex or an airport code in the search box and press Enter
Links to a view: the live map reads position, zoom, filters, units and the selected aircraft from the address, and Copy Link to This View builds one
Altitude chart and Export KML on the aircraft details card
Wide / Narrow button for the details card, a hover block on aircraft, a geometric-altitude label field and Reset My Map Settings
This Release Notes page
improved: Admin > Status says why a service failed, and its overall banner counts every row

The How to Feed page now says plainly that ultrafeeder users need nothing extra for MLAT, and explains UAT correctly: a station's 978 MHz aircraft travel through its normal feed, so no extra line, port or setting is needed
Data Source filter and the aircraft card treat UAT and ADS-R as one source, as the hub reports them
fixed: The stack updater clears a leftover parked container and retries, which fixes the 'portal FAILED' row on Admin > Status
A test that used a fixed date stopped working when the date arrived

title: MLAT everywhere, service status, new feed page
added: MLAT Network page: stations on a map, click one to see the stations it is synchronised with, coloured by how well their clocks agree
How an aircraft is tracked: the details card says whether the position came from ADS-B, MLAT, UAT/ADS-R, TIS-B or Mode S only, explains it, and for MLAT shows how many stations hear it
MLAT status in plain words on My Station (with what to fix), the public Feeders list and station pages, the public API, the feed check and the admin pages
Service Status pages: a plain-words page for everyone (/status) and an in-depth one for administrators with the reason behind each state
Data Source filter on the live map (ADS-B, MLAT, UAT/ADS-R, TIS-B, Mode S, other) with live counts
The hub itself is now managed by the stack updater, with the MLAT results input connected
improved: The How to Feed page was rewritten: how ADS-B, MLAT and UAT work, setup for new and existing stations, ports, troubleshooting and privacy
Nginx Proxy Manager is told to reload after any service is replaced, so a replaced container is never answered with a stale address

title: Stack updater and MLAT server
added: Stack updater (adsb-stack): one service that keeps every hub service in step with the compose files carried in its image, so new services appear on the hub with Update Now and no commands
MLAT server (adsb-mlat) running the upstream mlat-server, with Admin > MLAT showing connected stations and their health (never their locations)
improved: Update Now asks the stack updater to apply new services before Watchtower replaces images
Flight Progress draws the right aircraft shape for each type instead of one generic icon

title: Secrets and privacy hardening
security: Two-factor secrets and webhook addresses are stored sealed, recovery codes are keyed, backups are encrypted
Unknown user names at sign-in are masked, an emergency command-line tool exists for administrators, and a privacy crawl test checks that exact locations are never published

title: Two-factor sign-in
added: Two-factor sign-in with an authenticator app, ten one-time recovery codes, administrator reset and a setting to require it for administrators
fixed: Sky View no longer steps backward between position reports

title: Alert webhooks and sign-in security
added: Alert webhooks for Discord, Slack, ntfy or any JSON receiver, with limits and protection against unsafe addresses, so alerts work without email
security: A list of your sign-ins with Sign Out per device, a per-address sign-in throttle, browser security headers, and an audit entry when an administrator signs in from a new address

title: Flight History
added: Flight History: the portal keeps its own log of every flight it hears, with a History page, period pickers and earlier-flight tracks; the live map's search suggests earlier flights
Station statistics links with a Station selector, and the Network Feeders dashboard in the Tools menu
improved: Highlight for aircraft matching your alert rules, a Watch This Aircraft button, a station coverage layer and airport weather (METAR) on airport markers
More reliable release script

title: Sky View and weather updates
added: Sky View: a live 3D view from an aircraft with terrain, drag to look around, click another aircraft to jump to it, aircraft drawn at their true altitude, and a heading tape
Weather layers update automatically, with an Update Now button and an updated time per layer
fixed: Sky View no longer rewinds between reports

title: Weather panel
added: Weather panel with a tile for each layer, live preview, opacity slider, a 50-minute NEXRAD radar loop and winds aloft worked out from aircraft readings

title: Airline logos and military emblems
added: Real airline logos and real military service emblems on the live map, in the list (Airline column), on Flight Search and on Flight Progress
improved: Grafana dashboards

How to Feed guide with an Am I Feeding check

The live map built in: classic aircraft icons, columns, filters, a full details card with photo, make and model and route, trails, layers from tar1090's sources, radar, an Arkansas chart background and per-station views
